title.raw: Understanding Lymphedema Therapy and the Role of Certified Lymphedema Therapists
title.rendered: Understanding Lymphedema Therapy and the Role of Certified Lymphedema Therapists

content.raw:
Short answer: Lymphedema therapy usually combines education, skin care, exercise, compression, and sometimes manual lymphatic drainage or bandaging. The aim is long-term control, fewer infections and better function, not a guaranteed cure.

Clinically reviewed by Dr Jeremy Sun Mingfa, Plastic, Reconstructive & Lymphedema Surgeon in Singapore. Last reviewed: August 2026. This article is for education only and does not replace personalised medical assessment.

Core parts of therapy

  • Skin care to prevent cracks, fungal infection and cellulitis.
  • Exercise and breathing to support the muscle pump.
  • Compression garments or bandaging when prescribed.
  • Manual lymphatic drainage in selected patients.
  • Self-management skills for travel, work and flare prevention.

Intensive and maintenance phases

Some patients need an intensive phase with frequent therapy and bandaging to reduce swelling. Others mainly need maintenance with garments, exercise, monitoring and periodic refitting.

When therapy should be reviewed

Review is needed if garments become painful, swelling progresses, cellulitis recurs, or the patient cannot maintain the routine. Persistent symptoms despite good therapy may justify specialist imaging or surgical discussion.

Therapy and LVA/LVB

Microsurgery does not replace all conservative care. In suitable patients, LVA/LVB may improve drainage enough to reduce symptoms or compression burden, but ongoing monitoring remains important.

Frequently asked questions

What is complete decongestive therapy?

It is a structured programme combining compression, skin care, exercise, education and sometimes manual lymphatic drainage.

How long does therapy take?

It varies by stage, cause and severity. Many patients need long-term maintenance.

When should I see a lymphedema surgeon?

Consider review when swelling remains troublesome despite appropriate conservative care or infections recur.

Related surgical guide: If swelling remains persistent despite appropriate conservative care, or if recurrent cellulitis is a major issue, read LVA surgery in Singapore: lymphovenous bypass for lymphedema.
